contents.html_ja: VoIP システムは、従来の電話の受話器、会議用装置、モバイル装置など、さまざまな形態をとります。エンドユーザー機器に加えて、VoIP システムには、呼処理装置／コールマネージャー、ゲートウェイ、ルーター、ファイアウォール、プロトコルなど、さまざまな他の構成要素が含まれます。これらの構成要素の大半には、データネットワークで使われる対応物がありますが、VoIP の性能要求のため、通常のネットワークソフトウェアとハードウェアには、VoIP 専用の構成要素を追加しなければなりません。VoIP は、ほとんどのデータシステムより高い性能を必要とするだけでなく、緊急通報 911 などの重要なサービスにも対応しなければなりません。VoIP に不慣れな人が混乱する主な原因の一つは、デジタル化された音声が他のデータと同様にパケットで伝送されるのだから、既存のネットワークアーキテクチャとツールを変更なしで使えるはずだという（自然な）思い込みです。しかし、VoIP は既存のネットワーク技術にいくつもの複雑さを加え、セキュリティ上の考慮によって、これらの問題はいっそう深刻になります。
contents.html: VoIP systems take a wide variety of forms, including traditional telephone handsets, conferencing units, and mobile units. In addition to end-user equipment, VoIP systems include a variety of other components, including call processors/call managers, gateways, routers, firewalls, and protocols. Most of these components have counterparts used in data networks, but the performance demands of VoIP mean that ordinary network software and hardware must be supplemented with special VoIP components. Not only does VoIP require higher performance than most data systems, but critical services, such as Emergency 911, must be accommodated. One of the main sources of confusion for those new to VoIP is the (natural) assumption that because digitized voice travels in packets just like other data, existing network architectures and tools can be used without change. However, VoIP adds a number of complications to existing network technology, and these problems are magnified by security considerations.

contents.html: Quality of Service (QoS) is fundamental to the operation of a VoIP network that meets users’ quality expectations. However, the implementation of various security measures can cause a marked deterioration in QoS unless VoIP-specific equipment and architectures are used. These complications range from firewalls delaying or blocking call setups to encryption-produced latency and delay variation (jitter). Because of the time-critical nature of VoIP and its low tolerance for disruption and packet loss, many security measures implemented in traditional data networks are simply not applicable to VoIP in their current form; firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and other components must be specialized for VoIP. Most current VoIP systems use one of two standards—H.323 or the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP). Although SIP seems to be gaining in popularity, neither of these protocols has become dominant in the market yet, so it often makes sense to incorporate components that can support both.
contents.html_ja: サービス品質（QoS）は、ユーザーの品質への期待を満たす VoIP ネットワークの動作の基本です。しかし、VoIP 専用の機器とアーキテクチャを使わない限り、さまざまなセキュリティ対策の実施が QoS の顕著な低下を招くことがあります。これらの複雑さには、ファイアウォールが呼の設定を遅らせたり阻止したりすること、暗号化によって生じるレイテンシと遅延の変動（ジッタ）などがあります。VoIP は時間的な制約が厳しく、中断やパケット損失への耐性が低いため、従来のデータネットワークで実施されている多くのセキュリティ対策は、現状の形ではそのまま VoIP に適用できません。ファイアウォール、侵入検知システム、その他の構成要素は、VoIP 向けに特化しなければなりません。現在の VoIP システムの大半は、H.323 か Session Initiation Protocol（SIP）のいずれかの標準を使用しています。SIP は人気を集めているようですが、どちらのプロトコルもまだ市場で支配的にはなっていないため、両方に対応できる構成要素を組み込むことが理にかなっている場合が多くあります。

contents.html_ja: VoIP の導入により、セキュリティの必要性は増しています。今や、かけがえのない 2 つの資産、つまりデータと音声を保護しなければならないからです。連邦政府機関は、非機密であっても、多くの情報を保護することが法律で求められています。プライバシーに敏感なデータと財務データのほか、機微だが非機密（sensitive but unclassified）に分類される政府のその他の情報も保護しなければなりません。したがって、会話のセキュリティを保護することが求められます。従来のオフィスの電話システムでは、会話を傍受するには、電話回線への物理的なアクセスか、オフィスの構内交換機（PBX）の危殆化が必要です。従来の電話回線で音声トラフィックをわざわざ暗号化するのは、特にセキュリティに敏感な組織だけです。インターネットベースの接続については、同じことは言えません。たとえば、電話で商品を注文するとき、ほとんどの人は、クレジットカード番号を相手に読み上げます。番号は暗号化されずに販売者に送信されます。これに対し、暗号化されていないデータをインターネット経由で送信するリスクはより大きいです。ユーザーの自宅のコンピュータからオンライン小売業者に送られるパケットは、ユーザーの ISP や小売業者の管理下にない 15～20 のシステムを通過する場合があります。これらのシステムにアクセスできる者なら誰でも、クレジットカード情報を探してパケットをスキャンするソフトウェアをインストールできます。このため、オンライン小売業者は、ユーザーの情報とクレジットカード番号を保護するために暗号化ソフトウェアを使用します。したがって、インターネットプロトコルで、特にインターネット経由で音声を送信するのであれば、同様のセキュリティ対策を適用しなければならないのは当然です。
contents.html: With the introduction of VoIP, the need for security is compounded because now we must protect two invaluable assets—our data and our voice. Federal agencies are required by law to protect a great deal of information, even if it is unclassified. Both privacy-sensitive and financial data must be protected, as well as other government information that is categorized as sensitive but unclassified. Protecting the security of conversations is thus required. In a conventional office telephone system, intercepting conversations requires physical access to telephone lines or compromise of the office private branch exchange (PBX). Only particularly security-sensitive organizations bother to encrypt voice traffic over traditional telephone lines. The same cannot be said for Internet-based connections. For example, when ordering merchandise over the telephone, most people will read their credit card number to the person on the other end. The numbers are transmitted without encryption to the seller. In contrast, the risk of sending unencrypted data across the Internet is more significant. Packets sent from a user’s home computer to an online retailer may pass through 15 to 20 systems that are not under the control of the user’s ISP or the retailer. Anyone with access to these systems could install software that scans packets for credit card information. For this reason, online retailers use encryption software to protect a user’s information and credit card number. So it stands to reason that if we are to transmit voice over the Internet Protocol, and specifically across the Internet, similar security measures must be applied.

contents.html_ja: 現在のインターネットアーキテクチャは、電話回線と同じ物理的な配線のセキュリティを提供しません。VoIP を保護する鍵は、データネットワークで展開されているセキュリティ機構（ファイアウォール、暗号化など）を使って、PSTN ネットワークのユーザーが現在享受しているセキュリティ水準を再現することです。
contents.html: The current Internet architecture does not provide the same physical wire security as the telephone lines. The key to securing VoIP is to use the security mechanisms like those deployed in data networks (firewalls, encryption, etc.) to emulate the security level currently enjoyed by PSTN network users.

contents.html_ja: VoIP は安全に行うことができますが、その道のりは平坦ではありません。標準の問題が解決され、VoIP システムが主流の日用品になるまでには、おそらく数年かかるでしょう。それまでは、組織は慎重に進めなければならず、VoIP の構成要素が、ローカルネットワークの周辺機器がもう一つ増えるだけだと考えてはなりません。何よりも、VoIP 固有の要件に留意し、VoIP のセキュリティの課題に対応する適切なハードウェアとソフトウェアを入手することが重要です。
contents.html: VoIP can be done securely, but the path is not smooth. It will likely be several years before standards issues are settled and VoIP systems become a mainstream commodity. Until then, organizations must proceed cautiously and not assume that VoIP components are just more peripherals for the local network. Above all, it is important to keep in mind the unique requirements of VoIP, acquiring the right hardware and software to meet the challenges of VoIP security.

contents.html_ja: 昨年、CSD は、2005 年 1 月に公表された SP 800-58『Security Considerations for Voice Over IP Systems』の更新に取り組みました。この刊行物は、VoIP に関連する攻撃と防御を調査し、妥当なコストで VoIP ネットワークに適切な水準のセキュリティを提供する方法を探っています。公開以来、この刊行物は 120 万回を超えてダウンロードされています。更新された刊行物は、技術の変化、セキュリティ上の弱点につながり得るプロトコル機能間の潜在的な相互作用、標準の改訂、インターネット上の動画など、VoIP と関連技術の新たな応用を反映します。
contents.html: During the past year, CSD has worked toward an update of SP 800-58, Security Considerations for Voice Over IP Systems, which was published in January 2005. This publication investigates the attacks and defenses relevant to VoIP and explores ways to provide appropriate levels of security for VoIP networks at reasonable cost. More than 1.2 million copies of the publication have been downloaded since its release. The updated publication will reflect changes in technology, potential interactions between protocol features that could result in security weaknesses, revisions of standards, and new applications of VoIP and related technologies, such as video over Internet.

contents.html_ja: Web サービス技術の進歩は、インターネットとエンタープライズネットワークに広範な影響を与えると見込まれています。eXtensible Markup Language（XML）、Simple Object Access Protocol（SOAP）、関連するオープン標準に基づき、サービス指向アーキテクチャ（SOA）に展開される Web サービスは、動的かつアドホックな接続を通じて、人手を介さずにデータとアプリケーションが相互作用できるようにします。Web サービス技術は、さまざまなアーキテクチャに実装でき、他の技術やソフトウェア設計のアプローチと共存でき、レガシーアプリケーションやデータベースに大きな変革を求めることなく、段階的に導入できます。
contents.html: The advance of Web services technologies promises to have far-reaching effects on the Internet and enterprise networks. Web services based on the eXtensible Markup Language (XML), Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP), and related open standards, and deployed in Service Oriented Architectures (SOAs) allow data and applications to interact without human intervention through dynamic and ad hoc connections. Web services technology can be implemented in a wide variety of architectures, can coexist with other technologies and software design approaches, and can be adopted in an evolutionary manner without requiring major transformations to legacy applications and databases.

This publication was issued in order to improve the understanding of different aspects of Web services security. This document discusses the different technologies and standards for securing Web services applications. It also provides some specific recommendations that Web services application developers and architects can use to secure their applications.

contents.html_ja: 多くの組織やユーザーが、無線通信とデバイスは便利で柔軟性が高く、使いやすいことに気づいています。無線ローカルエリアネットワーク（WLAN）または Wi-Fi デバイスのユーザーは、ネットワークとの接続性を維持しながら、場所から場所へ移動できる柔軟性を得ています。Wi-Fi は Wireless Fidelity の略で、今日広く使われている Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers（IEEE）802.11 標準に基づく WLAN 製品の動作認証です。無線パーソナルエリアネットワーク（WPAN）により、ユーザーは、プリンターケーブルやその他の周辺機器の接続に縛られることなく、互換性のあるデバイスを持つネットワークシステムや他のユーザーとデータやアプリケーションを共有できます。PDA や携帯電話などの携帯デバイスのユーザーは、PDA とパーソナルコンピュータの間でデータを同期でき、無線電子メール、Web ブラウジング、インターネットアクセスなどのネットワークサービスを利用できます。さらに、無線通信は、緊急事態の対応要員が重要な情報を入手し、取り組みを調整し、他の方法が対応能力を超えたり機能しなくなったりした場合にも通信を維持するのに役立ちます。
contents.html: Many organizations and users have found that wireless communications and devices are convenient, flexible, and easy to use. Users of wireless local area network (WLAN) or Wi-Fi devices have the flexibility to move from one place to another while maintaining connectivity with the network. Wi-Fi, short for Wireless Fidelity, is an operability certification for WLAN products based on the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.11 standard that is widely used today. Wireless personal area networks (WPANs) allow users to share data and applications with network systems and other users with compatible devices without being tied to printer cables and other peripheral device connections. Users of handheld devices such as PDAs and cellular phones can synchronize data between PDAs and personal computers, and can use network services such as wireless e-mail, Web browsing, and Internet access. Further, wireless communications can help first responders to emergencies gain critical information, coordinate efforts, and keep communications working when other methods may be overwhelmed or are nonfunctioning.

contents.html_ja: 無線ネットワークは、有線ネットワークと同じリスクの多くにさらされる一方で、それ以外のリスクにも脆弱です。無線ネットワークは無線周波数でデータを送信するため、保護しなければ侵入者に対して開かれています。侵入者はこの開放性を悪用して、システムにアクセスし、データを破壊または窃取し、ネットワーク帯域を占有して許可されたユーザーへのサービスを拒否する攻撃を仕掛けてきました。
contents.html: While wireless networks are exposed to many of the same risks as wired networks, they are vulnerable to additional risks as well. Wireless networks transmit data through radio frequencies and are open to intruders unless protected. Intruders have exploited this openness to access systems, destroy and steal data, and launch attacks that tie up network bandwidth and deny service to authorized users.

contents.html: This past year, we completed two Special Publications dealing with wireless security issues. The first, SP 800-97, Establishing Wireless Robust Security Networks: A Guide to IEEE 802.11i, provides readers with a detailed explanation of next-generation 802.11 wireless security. It describes the inherently flawed Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) and explains 802.11i’s two-step approach (interim and long-term) to providing effective wireless security. It describes secure methods used to authenticate users in a wireless environment and presents several sample case studies of wireless deployment. It also includes guidance on best practices for establishing secure wireless networks using the emerging Wi-Fi technology. This SP was published in February 2007.
contents.html_ja: 昨年は、無線セキュリティの問題を扱う 2 つの特別刊行物を完成させました。1 つ目の SP 800-97『Establishing Wireless Robust Security Networks: A Guide to IEEE 802.11i』は、次世代の 802.11 無線セキュリティについて、読者に詳しい説明を提供します。本質的に欠陥のある Wired Equivalent Privacy（WEP）を説明し、効果的な無線セキュリティを提供するための 802.11i の 2 段階のアプローチ（暫定的なものと長期的なもの）を解説します。無線環境でユーザーを認証するために使われる安全な方法を説明し、無線展開のいくつかのケーススタディの例を示します。また、新たに登場する Wi-Fi 技術を使って安全な無線ネットワークを構築するためのベストプラクティスのガイダンスも含まれます。この SP は 2007 年 2 月に公表されました。

contents.html_ja: 無線セキュリティに関する 2 つ目の刊行物は、2007 年 8 月にパブリックコメント用に公開されました。SP 800-48 改訂第 1 版『Wireless Network Security for IEEE 802.11a/b/g and Bluetooth』は、2002 年に公表された SP 800-48 の初版を更新するものです。WEP の弱点を補うための追加のセキュリティ管理策の使用を含め、古い 802.11 ネットワーク（802.11i 以前）を保護するための推奨を示します。また、Bluetooth としてよく知られる WPAN プロトコルの IEEE 802.15.1 のセキュリティ機能についても論じ、これらのセキュリティ機能を使って Bluetooth の通信を一般的な攻撃から保護する方法を説明します。
contents.html: The second publication on wireless security was released for public comment in August 2007. SP 800-48 Revision 1, Wireless Network Security for IEEE 802.11a/b/g and Bluetooth, is an update to the original version of SP 800-48, which was published in 2002. It provides recommendations on securing older 802.11 networks (pre-802.11i), including the use of additional security controls to compensate for WEP’s weaknesses. It also discusses the security features of the WPAN protocol IEEE 802.15.1, better known as Bluetooth, and explains how these security features can be used to protect Bluetooth communications from common attacks.

contents.html_ja: 生体認証技術は、身体的または行動的な特徴の認識に基づいて、以前に登録された個人に対して、個人の身元を確立し、または検証できます。身体的特徴の例には、手、指、顔、虹彩があります。行動的特徴は、動的署名検証やキーストロークダイナミクスのように、学習または獲得された特性です。人間の識別に生体認証を使うことには、あなたをあなたとして識別できるのは生体情報だけであるという、独自の利点があります。生体認証技術は、単独で、またはトークンなどの他の認証技術と併用すると、他の技術を単独で用いるよりも高い水準のセキュリティを提供でき、他の技術の弱点を克服するためにも使えます。数十年にわたり、生体認証技術は主に法執行のアプリケーションで使われてきており、現在もこれらの重要なアプリケーションの主要な構成要素です。ここ数年で、生体認証ソリューションの市場は大幅に拡大しました。現在では、人物の身元を検証し、国境を守り、建物やコンピュータネットワークを含む安全な場所へのアクセスを制限するために、世界中の公的部門と民間部門の複数のアプリケーションで、ますます利用されています。
contents.html: Biometric technologies are able to establish or verify personal identity against previously enrolled individuals based upon recognition of a physiological or behavioral characteristic. Examples of biological characteristics include hand, finger, facial, and iris. Behavioral characteristics are traits that are learned or acquired, such as dynamic signature verification and keystroke dynamics. Using biometrics for identifying human beings offers some unique advantages because only biometrics can identify you as you. Used alone, or together with other authentication technologies such as tokens, biometric technologies can provide higher degrees of security than other technologies employed alone and can also be used to overcome their weaknesses. For decades, biometric technologies were used primarily in law enforcement applications, and they are still a key component of these important applications. Over the past several years, the marketplace for biometrics solutions has widened significantly. Currently, they are increasingly being used in multiple public and private sector applications worldwide to verify a person’s identity, secure national borders, and restrict access to secure sites including buildings and computer networks.

contents.html_ja: 生体認証に基づくソリューションの市場が大幅に拡大するにつれ、これらの生体認証技術の重要性も劇的に高まりました。国土安全保障は、多くの国にとって最優先事項です。生体認証に基づくソリューションは、これらのアプリケーションで重要な役割を果たしています。生体認証技術は、身分証明書、ポイントプログラム、福祉プログラムの管理に関連するもの、遊園地、銀行、モバイルデバイス、パスポートプログラム、運転免許証、大学や学校の給食プログラムなど、多様な環境に見られます。National Science and Technology Council（NSTC）の Subcommittee on Biometrics and Identity Management が作成した National Biometric Challenge 文書に述べられているとおり、「生体認証は、現在利用可能な最も決定的でリアルタイムの ID 管理ツールです」。<sup>1</sup>
contents.html: As the marketplace for biometric-based solutions has widened significantly, the importance of these biometric technologies has also dramatically increased. Homeland security is the highest priority for many countries. Biometric-based solutions play an important role in these applications. Biometric technologies can be found in identification cards, loyalty programs, associated with the management of welfare programs, and in such diverse environments as amusement parks, banks, mobile devices, passport programs, driver’s licenses, and college and school lunch programs. As stated in the National Biometric Challenge document developed by the National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) Subcommittee on Biometrics and Identity Management, “biometrics are the most definitive, real-time identity management tools currently available.”<sup>1</sup>

contents.html_ja: 政府のユーザーとその他の消費者は、生体認証に基づく、高性能で相互運用可能な、標準に基づく情報システムを必要としています。オープンシステムの標準が適時に利用できない場合、ユーザーは専有のソリューションの採用を選ぶ可能性があります。これらの専有システムから標準に基づくオープンシステムのソリューションへの移行は、通常、困難で費用がかかります。国土安全保障、ID 窃盗の防止、その他の政府・商業アプリケーションのために、これらの新しい情報技術システムを展開するには、生体認証について、国内および国際的な合意標準が必要です。これらの生体認証標準は、顧客が生体認証に基づくオープンシステムのソリューションを使って、個人の検証・識別のアプリケーションで、より高い水準のセキュリティと相互運用性を達成するのを助けることにより、生体認証技術の大衆市場での採用を支えます。したがって、生体認証に関する国家戦略と、これらの標準および適合性試験アーキテクチャなどの関連する試験技術の策定を支援することが、当部門の生体認証標準プログラムの礎石です。
contents.html: Government users and other consumers need biometric-based, high-performance, interoperable, standards-based information systems. In the absence of the timely availability of open systems standards, users may choose to adopt proprietary solutions. Migration from these proprietary systems to standards-based open-system solutions is usually difficult and expensive. Deploying these new information technology systems for homeland security, for preventing ID theft, and for other government and commercial applications requires national and international consensus standards for biometrics. These biometric standards support the mass-market adoption of biometric technologies by helping customers to achieve higher levels of security and interoperability in personal verification and identification applications using biometric-based, open-systems solutions. Therefore, supporting the national strategy on biometrics and the development of these standards and related testing technology such as conformance testing architectures is the cornerstone of our biometrics standards program.

contents.html_ja: 私たちは、公式な国内・国際の生体認証標準と関連する適合性評価の策定を加速し、これらの標準に基づくオープンシステムのソリューションの能力についてユーザーを教育し、その採用を促進し、必要な適合性試験ツールでこれらの標準を支援することにより、オープンシステムの標準に対する政府と市場の要求に応えています。この戦略は、必要な生体認証標準と、関連する研究、技術開発、試験の策定を、包括的に特定し計画することを求めます。
contents.html: We are responding to government and market requirements for open-systems standards by accelerating development of formal national and international biometric standards and associated conformity assessments, educating their users on the capability of these standards-based open-systems solutions, by promoting their adoption and by supporting these standards with the required conformance test tools. This strategy requires comprehensively identifying and planning for the development of the required biometric standards and associated research and technology developments and testing.

contents.html: In order to meet these immediate government and private sector needs for high performance and highly secure open systems, in the past year we have worked in close partnership with other U.S. Government agencies and U.S. industry to establish standards bodies for accelerating the development of formal national and international biometric standards of high relevance to the nation. We are an active participant on NSTC’s Subcommittee on Biometrics and Identity Management. NIST experts also participate in its Standards and Conformity Assessment Working Group (SCA WG).
contents.html_ja: 高性能で安全性の高いオープンシステムに対する、政府と民間部門のこれらの差し迫ったニーズを満たすため、昨年は、他の米国政府機関と米国産業界と緊密に連携して、国にとって関連性の高い、公式な国内・国際の生体認証標準の策定を加速するための標準化団体を設立しました。NSTC の Subcommittee on Biometrics and Identity Management に積極的に参加しています。NIST の専門家は、その Standards and Conformity Assessment Working Group（SCA WG）にも参加しています。

contents.html_ja: 当部門のプログラムは、2006 年 8 月に公表された NSTC の National Biometrics Challenge 文書の目標、および生体認証標準の策定、採用、使用を可能にするためのポリシーを示す、NSTC が最近発行した文書の原則と目標とよく整合し、それらを支えています。<sup>2</sup> これらの共通の目標には、国家の安全保障と米国を拠点とするコミュニティの安定に不可欠な、生体認証の自主的な合意標準の継続的な策定の支援と、ベンダーとシステムが生体認証標準に準拠していることを確保するために必要な、厳格な試験を支える技術開発が含まれます。当部門のプログラムの専門家は、NIST/ITL および ITL の Information Access Division の生体認証の専門家と緊密に連携して取り組んでいます。このプログラムは、生体認証の標準化と生体認証標準の採用の大きな触媒と見なされており、その業績により国内外で評価を得ています（2007 会計年度に、生体認証標準プログラムの責任者である Fernando Podio は、ANSI Federation と自主的な標準化コミュニティへの多大な貢献を称えて、ANSI Meritorious Service Award を受賞しました）。
contents.html: Our program is well aligned to and supports the goals of NSTC’s National Biometrics Challenge document released in August 2006, as well as the principles and goals of NSTC’s recently issued document delineating policy for enabling the development, adoption, and use of biometric standards.<sup>2</sup> These common goals include support for the continued development of voluntary consensus standards for biometrics vital to the security of the nation and the stability of the U.S.-based community and technology development in support of rigorous testing that is required to ensure vendor and system compliance with biometric standards. Our program experts work in close collaboration with the NIST/ITL and ITL’s Information Access Division’s biometric experts. This program is considered to be a major catalyst for biometric standardization and adoption of biometric standards and has gained national and international recognition for its achievements. (During Fiscal Year 2007, the biometric standards program lead, Fernando Podio, was a recipient of the ANSI Meritorious Service Award in recognition of his many contributions to the ANSI Federation and the voluntary standardization community.)

contents.html_ja: 標準が存在するだけでは、製品が標準に定められた技術要件を満たしていることを示すには十分ではありません。適合性試験は、仕様の技術的な記述を捉え、実装が仕様を忠実に実装しているかどうかを測定します。適合性テストスイートの実装は、仕様や標準に記述された試験方法論への適合性を確認するために使われる試験ソフトウェアです。私たちは、これらの標準の策定への積極的な技術面での参加、特定の生体認証標準プロジェクト（たとえば、生体認証の技術インタフェースの適合性試験方法論）の後援、複数の生体認証標準への適合性を試験するために設計された関連する適合性試験アーキテクチャの開発を通じて、国内・国際の生体認証標準と適合性評価の策定を支援しています。BioAPI 仕様や、Common Biometric Exchange Format Framework（CBEFF）標準に準拠する Biometric Information Record などの、主要な生体認証インタフェース標準の採用と実装を支えるため、適合性テストスイートを開発してきました。これらのレコードは、含まれる生体データに関連するメタデータのほか、あらゆるモダリティの生体データ、セキュリティおよび完全性のデータを運ぶことができます。
contents.html: The existence of standards alone is not enough to demonstrate that products meet the technical requirements specified in the standards. Conformance testing captures the technical description of a specification and measures whether an implementation faithfully implements the specification. A conformance test suite implementation is test software that is used to ascertain conformance to a testing methodology described in a specification or standard. We support the development of national and international biometric standards and conformity assessment through active technical participation in the development of these standards, sponsorship of specific biometric standard projects (e.g., conformance testing methodologies for biometric technical interfaces), and the development of associated conformance testing architectures designed to test for conformance to a number of biometric standards. We have developed conformance test suites in support of the adoption and implementation of key biometric interface standards such as the BioAPI specification and Biometric Information Records conforming to Common Biometric Exchange Format Framework (CBEFF) standards. These records are able to transport metadata related to the biometric data that they contain as well as biometric data of any modality and security and integrity data.

contents.html_ja: 2006 年に、BioAPI 仕様である ANSI INCITS 358-2002 の実装を試験するために開発した Conformance Test Suite（CTS）を公開しました。生体認証標準を策定する国内委員会（InterNational Committee for Information Technology Standards – INCITS M1）の他のメンバーとともに、BioAPI の適合性試験方法論の標準を共同で後援しました。この標準は 2007 年中に完成し、米国国家標準として公表される予定です。CTS の実装は、適合性試験方法論の標準に規定された概念と原則を使って開発されました。この CTS は、BioAPI 標準への適合を主張する、さまざまなモダリティ（たとえば、顔、虹彩、指紋の認識）の、市販のベンダーの生体認証サブシステムを用いて、徹底的に試験されました。試験結果は、DoD の Biometric Task Force が独自に開発した別の同様の CTS と、うまく相互検証されました。NSTC の Subcommittee on Biometrics and Identity Management は、BioAPI CTS の開発を 2006 年の「Technology Successes」の一つに挙げました。
contents.html: In 2006 we released a Conformance Test Suite (CTS) developed to test implementations of ANSI INCITS 358-2002, the BioAPI specification. We cosponsored with other members of the national committee developing biometric standards (InterNational Committee for Information Technology Standards – INCITS M1) a conformance testing methodology standard for BioAPI. This standard was completed during 2007 and is about to be published as an American National Standard. The CTS implementation was developed using concepts and principles specified in the conformance testing methodology standard. This CTS was thoroughly tested with a number of commercially available vendor biometric subsystems for different modalities (e.g., face, iris and fingerprint recognition) claiming conformance to the BioAPI standard. The test results were successfully cross-validated with another similar CTS independently developed by DoD’s Biometric Task Force. The NSTC Subcommittee on Biometrics and Identity Management listed the BioAPI CTS developments as one of the “Technology Successes” of 2006.

contents.html_ja: 2007 年中に、CBEFF 生体認証情報レコード（BIR）を試験するための試験アーキテクチャと CTS の実装の開発を完了しました。この適合性試験アーキテクチャは、これらの BIR の 3 つの構成要素の CTS を支えます。その構成要素は、(1) レコードに含まれる生体データに関するメタデータ（作成者、有効期間、生体データのモダリティと形式、生体認証製品の識別子、データ構造に採用されたセキュリティと完全性のオプションなど）を含む CBEFF ヘッダ、(2) 生体データを含む Biometric Data Block、(3) 完全性／暗号化の情報を含む署名／セキュリティブロックです。さらに、CBEFF BIR の構造の 3 つの要素の CTS 試験モジュールを支えるよう設計された、高度な Conformance Testing Suite アーキテクチャの初期バージョンを開発しました。この実験的なアーキテクチャは、これらの BIR の 3 つの構成要素のローカル試験と、Web サービスを通じたこれらの BIR の構成要素のリモート試験を可能にします。
contents.html: During 2007, we completed the development of a testing architecture and a CTS implementation to test CBEFF Biometric Information Records (BIR). The conformance testing architecture supports CTS for the three components of these BIRs including: (1) CBEFF headers, which contain metadata on the biometric data contained in the record such as the creator, validity period, biometric modality and format on the biometric data, the biometric product identifier, and the security and integrity options adopted for the data structure; (2) the Biometric Data Block, which contains the biometric data; and (3) Signature/security block, which contains integrity/encryption information. In addition, we developed the initial version of an advanced Conformance Testing Suite architecture that was designed to support CTS testing modules for the three elements of a CBEFF BIRs structure. This experimental architecture allows local testing of the three components of these BIRs as well as remote testing of the components of these BIR through Web services.

contents.html: We have continued to participate in related consortia efforts such as the U.S. Biometrics Consortium (BC). The BC currently consists of hundreds of members representing over 60 government agencies, industry, and academia. NIST cochairs the BC with NSA. The BC sponsors an annual conference and technical workshops. The BC 2007 conference was held at the Baltimore Convention Center in September. The two-and-a-half day conference, recognized by attendees as one of the largest conferences dedicated to biometrics worldwide, had over 100 speakers from government, industry, and academia, and over 1000 participants.

contents.html_ja: 2001 年後半に、当部門の生体認証標準プログラムは INCITS M1 の設立を支援しました。設立以来、INCITS M1 の目的は、国土防衛、ID 管理、ID 窃盗の防止、生体認証に基づくその他の政府・商業の個人検証または識別アプリケーションなど、米国のニーズにとって重要と考えられる分野について、公式な国内・国際の生体認証標準を迅速に策定・承認するため、米国で優先度の高い、焦点を絞った包括的なアプローチを確保することです。CSD は INCITS M1 の議長を務め、INCITS M1 の 5 つのタスクグループのうち 1 つの議長を出し、その標準の策定に積極的に参加しています。
contents.html: In late 2001, our biometric standards program helped establish INCITS M1. Since its inception, the purpose of INCITS M1 has been to ensure a high-priority focused and comprehensive approach in the United States for the rapid development and approval of formal national and international biometric standards, considered to be critical for U.S. needs, such as homeland defense, ID management, the prevention of identity theft, and for other government and commercial biometric-based personal verification or identification applications. CSD provides the Chair of INCITS M1, provides a Chair of one of the five INCITS M1 Task Groups, and actively participates in the development of its standards.

contents.html_ja: INCITS M1 は現在、元の標準を明確にし、技術革新と新しい顧客のニーズに対処し、音声データの新しいデータ交換フォーマットの策定に対処するため、生体データ交換フォーマット標準群の改訂／修正プロジェクトを進めています。INCITS M1 は、複数の生体データ交換フォーマットの適合性試験方法論標準も策定中です。上述のとおり、BioAPI 仕様や Common Biometric Exchange Frameworks Format（CBEFF）など、主要な生体認証の技術インタフェース標準の適合性試験方法論標準の策定を、INCITS M1 の他のメンバーとともに共同で後援しました。BioAPI の適合性試験方法論標準の策定は完了し、米国国家標準として承認される前の最終的な公開レビュー中です。CBEFF のインスタンス化に準拠する CBEFF Biometric Information Record の適合性試験方法論標準の策定は進行中です。INCITS M1 は、マルチ生体認証と生体融合データを支える標準、生体サンプル品質標準、データ交換フォーマット標準の生体認証の性能と相互運用性の試験を規定する標準の策定にも取り組んでいます。NIST の専門家は、これらすべての標準策定で非常に積極的に活動してきました。
contents.html: INCITS M1 is currently developing revision/amendment projects for its portfolio of biometric data interchange format standards to clarify original standards, address technology innovation and new customers’ needs, and address the development of a new data interchange format for voice data. INCITS M1 is also developing conformance testing methodology standards for a number of the biometric data interchange formats. As stated above, we cosponsored with other INCITS M1 members the development of conformance testing methodology standards for key biometric technical interface standards such as the BioAPI specification and the Common Biometric Exchange Frameworks Format (CBEFF). The development of the BioAPI conformance testing methodology standard was completed and is in final public review before approval as an American National Standard. Development of the conformance testing methodology standard for CBEFF Biometric Information Records conforming to CBEFF instantiations is underway. INCITS M1 is also addressing the development of standards to support multi-biometrics and biometric fusion data, a biometric sample quality standard, and a standard to specify biometric performance and interoperability testing of data interchange format standards. NIST experts have been very active in all of these standards developments.

contents.html_ja: 2002 年に、ISO/IEC 合同技術委員会 1（ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 37-Biometrics）のもとでの小委員会 37-生体認証の設立を成功裏に支援しました。INCITS M1 は、JTC1/SC 37 で米国を代表する責任を負う国内技術委員会です。CSD は SC37 の議長を提供し、NIST/ITL は、小委員会のもとで活動する 6 つのワーキンググループの一つの議長を務める人物を提供しています。
contents.html: In 2002, we successfully supported the establishment of Subcommittee 37-Biometrics under the ISO/IEC Joint Technical Committee 1 (ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 37-Biometrics). INCITS M1 is the national Technical Committee responsible for representing the U.S. in JTC1/SC 37. CSD provides the Chair of SC37, and NIST/ITL provides a person to serve as the Chair of one of the six Working Groups operating under the Subcommittee.

contents.html_ja: JTC 1/SC 37 の進行中の作業には、54 のサブプロジェクト（標準と技術報告書）に細分化された 15 のプロジェクトがあります。これには、元の標準を明確にし技術革新に対処するための、多くのデータ交換フォーマット標準と技術インタフェースの改訂と修正が含まれ、音声と DNA の 2 つの新しいデータ交換フォーマットの策定にも対処しています。2007 年中に、小委員会は、生体認証の性能試験のほか、相互運用性とデータ交換のための報告標準と生体認証プロファイルなど、他の生体認証標準の策定で大きく前進しました。JTC 1/SC 37 は、生体データ交換フォーマット標準（複数部構成の標準）に規定された生体データレコードの適合性試験方法論標準と、生体認証の使用に関する複数の管轄区域にまたがる側面についての複数部構成の技術報告書、および包括的で調和のとれた生体認証用語集の策定に着手しました。
contents.html: JTC 1/SC 37’s ongoing work includes 15 projects subdivided into 54 subprojects (standards and technical reports). They include revision and amendments of a number of data interchange format standards and technical interfaces to clarify original standards and to address technology innovations, and also address the development of two new data interchange formats for voice data and DNA. During 2007, the subcommittee made significant progress in the development of other biometric standards, including biometric performance testing, as well as reporting standards and biometric profiles for interoperability and data interchange. JTC 1/SC 37 has initiated the development of conformance testing methodology standards for the biometric data records specified in the biometric data interchange format standards (multi-part standard), as well as a multi-part technical report on cross-jurisdictional aspects of the use of biometrics, and a comprehensive harmonized biometric vocabulary.

contents.html_ja: NIST は、JTC 1/SC 37 の標準群の策定に非常に積極的に取り組んでいます。当部門の専門家は、政府、産業界、学界の他の米国国内委員会メンバーと協力して、生体認証技術と個人認識システムの技術革新を検討しています。国際的な生体認証標準の「第 2 世代」の策定を開始するための措置を講じました。標準策定団体は、既存の標準の機能を補完し強化し、新しい顧客のニーズを満たすための新たなプロジェクトを並行して検討しています。
contents.html: NIST is very active in the development of JTC 1/SC 37’s standards portfolio. Our experts, in collaboration with other U.S. national body members from government, industry, and academia, are examining innovations in biometrics technologies and personal recognition systems. We have taken steps to start the development of the “second generation” of international biometric standards. The standard development body is concurrently considering new projects to complement and enhance functionality of the existing standards and to meet new customers’ needs.

contents.html_ja: 「第 1 世代」の生体認証標準の多くは、すでに個人認証アプリケーションの顧客から求められています。国際民間航空機関（ICAO）（機械読取式旅行文書について）、国連の国際労働事務局（船員身分証明書プログラムについて）などの大規模な組織や、欧州連合（EU）は、JTC 1/SC 37 が策定した国際的な生体認証標準の使用を含む要件を公表しています。EU パスポート仕様の作業文書は、加盟国が発行するパスポートと旅行文書のセキュリティ機能と生体認証の標準に関する EU 理事会規則に基づく、IC チップ搭載 EU パスポートのソリューションを記述しています。この仕様は、国際標準、特に ISO 標準と機械読取式旅行文書に関する ICAO の勧告に依拠しており、生体の顔と指紋の識別子の仕様を含んでいます。したがって、この仕様は、JTC 1/SC 37 の作業から生まれた ISO 標準によって裏付けられています。JTC 1/SC 37 の複数の国内委員会が、小委員会が策定した特定の国際標準を参照しています。たとえば、スペインの電子パスポートは、JTC 1/SC 37 が策定した顔画像認識に基づく顔画像データを必要としています。
contents.html: A number of the “first generation” biometric standards are already being required by customers of personal authentication applications. Large organizations such as the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) (for Machine Readable Travel Documents), the International Labour Office of the United Nations (for the Seafarers Identification Credential program) as well as the European Union (EU) have published requirements that include the use of international biometric standards developed by JTC 1/SC 37. The EU password specification working document describes solutions for chip-enabled EU passports, based on EU’s Council Regulation on standards for security features and biometrics in passports and travel documents issued by member states. The specification relies on international standards, especially ISO standards and ICAO recommendations on Machine Readable Travel Documents, and includes specifications for biometric face and fingerprint identifiers; thus, the specifications are underpinned by ISO standards resulting from the work of JTC 1/SC37. Several JTC 1/SC 37 national bodies refer to certain international standards developed by the subcommittee. Spanish e-Passports, for example, require face image data based on the face image recognition developed by JTC 1/SC 37.

contents.html: In the United States, several organizations require selected biometric data interchange standards developed by JTC 1/SC 37. Examples include applications and tests performed by government organizations, private industry, and consortia. The Transportation Security Administration (TSA), a part of DHS, has issued guidance for use of biometric technology in airport access control systems and is performing tests to establish a qualified products list of biometric technologies which meet standards set forth in the aforementioned guidance. Products tested in TSA Qualified Product List (QPL) Testing include enrollment stations and biometric sensors/readers that can be deployed at access points to secure airport areas. The test requirements reference two parts of the multi-part standard developed by JTC 1/SC 37 on biometric performance testing and reporting. NIST used a part of this multi-part standard for the “Minutiae Interoperability Exchange Test (MINEX)” tests. The Registered Traveler Interoperability Consortium (RTIC) uses some of the JTC 1/SC 37 standards as well.
contents.html_ja: 米国では、複数の組織が、JTC 1/SC 37 が策定した特定の生体データ交換標準を必要としています。例には、政府組織、民間産業、コンソーシアムが実施するアプリケーションと試験があります。DHS の一部である運輸保安局（TSA）は、空港のアクセス制御システムでの生体認証技術の使用に関するガイダンスを発行しており、前述のガイダンスに定められた標準を満たす生体認証技術の適格製品一覧を確立するための試験を実施しています。TSA の Qualified Product List（QPL）試験で試験される製品には、空港の保安区域の出入口に展開できる登録端末と生体センサー／リーダーが含まれます。試験要件は、生体認証の性能試験と報告に関する JTC 1/SC 37 が策定した複数部構成の標準の 2 つの部を参照しています。NIST は、この複数部構成の標準の一部を「Minutiae Interoperability Exchange Test（MINEX）」の試験に使用しました。Registered Traveler Interoperability Consortium（RTIC）も、JTC 1/SC 37 の標準のいくつかを使用しています。

contents.html_ja: CS1 の範囲は、INCITS の B10、M1、T3、T10、T11 で現在進行中のサイバーセキュリティ標準化の作業分野と、Alliance for Telecommunications Industry Solutions、Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.、Internet Engineering Task Force、Travel Industry Association of American、Accredited Standards Committee（ASC）X9 などの他の標準化グループの作業分野を、明示的に除外しています。CS1 の作業範囲は、NIST のコンピュータセキュリティ部門が扱うサイバーセキュリティ分野と同じ分野の大半の標準化を含みます。
contents.html: The scope of CS1 explicitly excludes the areas of work on cyber security standardization presently underway in INCITS B10, M1, T3, T10 and T11; as well as other standard groups, such as the Alliance for Telecommunications Industry Solutions, the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc., the Internet Engineering Task Force, the Travel Industry Association of American, and Accredited Standards Committee (ASC) X9. The CS1 scope of work includes standardization in most of the same cyber security areas as are covered in the NIST Computer Security Division.

contents.html_ja: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 27 に対する米国 TAG として、CS1 は、IT セキュリティ技術に関する SC 27 の作業プログラムに、SC 27 の標準プロジェクトに関する用語、コメント、寄与を通じて貢献し、さまざまな策定段階にある SC 27 の標準文書に投票し、さまざまな SC 27 のプロジェクトに取り組む、またはさまざまな SC 27 のリーダーの職務に就く米国の専門家を特定しています。現在、CS1 のメンバー 9 名が、NIST の Randy Easter による ISO/IEC 24759『Test Requirements for Cryptographic Modules』を含め、さまざまな標準プロジェクトで SC 27 の文書編集者または共同編集者を務めています。CS1 のメンバー 1 名が、Study Period on Secure System Design のラポータを務めています。CS1 からのすべての入力は、INCITS を通じて ANSI に、そして SC 27 に送られます。また、米国発の新規作業項目提案と米国で策定された国家標準を、国際的な SC 27 の標準策定プロセスに取り込むための経路でもあります。CS1 は、技術的な情報システム管理監査、低電力暗号化、署名暗号化、三者間のエンティティ認証、責任ある脆弱性開示、セキュアなシステム設計に関する研究期間と新規作業項目提案を含め、SC 27 のいくつかの新たな作業分野に貢献しています。
contents.html: As the U.S. TAG to ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 27, CS1 contributes to the SC 27 program of work on IT Security Techniques in terms, comments, and contributions on SC 27 standards projects; votes on SC 27 standards documents at various stages of development; and identifying U.S. experts to work on various SC 27 projects or to serve in various SC 27 leadership positions. Currently 9 CS1 members are SC 27 document editors or coeditors on various standards projects, including Randy Easter of NIST for ISO/IEC 24759, Test Requirements for Cryptographic Modules. One CS1 member serves as Rapporteur for the Study Period on Secure System Design. All input from CS1 goes through INCITS to ANSI, then to SC 27. It is also a conduit for getting U.S.-based new work item proposals and U.S.-developed national standards into the international SC 27 standards development process. CS1 is making contributions on several new areas of work in SC 27, including study periods and new work item proposals on technical information system management audits, low power encryption, and signcryption, three-party entity authentication, responsible vulnerability disclosure, and secure system design.

contents.html_ja: CS1 のメンバーとして、Dan Benigni が投票権のない議長を務め、Richard Kissel が投票権を持つ NIST 主担当を務めており、NIST は CS1 のすべての国内・国際的な IT セキュリティ標準の取り組みに貢献しています。NIST はまた、CS1 のメンバーとして、国内または国際的な標準化のための IT セキュリティ関連のプロジェクトを開始することもできます。たとえば、CSD の職員の David Ferraiolo は最近、オペレーティングシステムに組み込めるアクセス制御機構に関する新しいプロジェクトを CS1 で開始することについて議論しました。Dan Benigni はまた、金融・保険サービス業界のセキュリティのニーズと要件を調査し、現在の標準と実務に欠けているものを評価し、これらの業界で展開可能なベストプラクティスとセキュリティの枠組みを作成するアプローチについて推奨を行うことを任務とする、INCITS の新しい Study Group on Security Best Practices への CS1 の連絡担当も務めています。
contents.html: Through its membership on CS1, where Dan Benigni serves as the nonvoting chair, and Richard Kissel is the NIST Primary with vote, NIST contributes to all CS1 national and international IT security standards efforts. NIST can also initiate IT security-related projects for national or international standardization through its membership on CS1. As an example, CSD staffer David Ferraiolo recently discussed initiating a new project in CS1 concerning an access control mechanism that can be embedded into operating systems. Dan Benigni also serves as CS1 Liaison to a new INCITS Study Group on Security Best Practices, whose charter is to study the security needs and requirements of the financial and insurance services industries, assess what is missing in current standards and practices, and make recommendations on an approach to create deployable best practices and frameworks for security in these industries.

contents.html_ja: CS1 は、CS1.1 RBAC というタスクグループを設置しており、「Requirements for the Implementation of Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)」INCITS Project 1794 という国内標準プロジェクトが 1 つあります。この標準は、INCITS 359-2004 で定義された RBAC の構成要素を使用する RBAC システムの実装要件を提供します。この標準の実装要件は、RBAC データ（たとえば、ロール、権限、ユーザー）の交換を確保し、RBAC のサービスとアプリケーション間の機能的な相互運用性を促進することを意図しています。今後数か月以内に、この作業は最初のパブリックレビューの準備が整います。
contents.html: CS1 has created a task group called CS1.1 RBAC, with one national standards project called “Requirements for the Implementation of Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)” INCITS Project 1794. This standard will provide implementation requirements for RBAC systems, which use RBAC components defined in INCITS 359-2004. The implementation requirements in this standard are intended to ensure the interchange of RBAC data (e.g., roles, permissions, users) and promote functional interoperability among RBAC services and applications. Within the next several months, this work will be ready for its first public review.

contents.html_ja: さらに、CS1 は最近、別の国内標準プロジェクトとして、「Minimum Security Guidelines for Protecting Personal Identifiable Information and Sensitive Information Stored on and Exchanged between Information Systems」を設置しました。このプロジェクトは、ANSI-INCITS の技術報告書となる見込みです。将来、この文書は SC 27 への入力文書として提出される可能性があります。この文書は、NIST SP 800 シリーズの特定の刊行物も考慮し、個人を特定できる情報の保護の範囲に当てはまる側面を取り入れます。
contents.html: In addition, CS1 has recently created another national standards project, “Minimum Security Guidelines for Protecting Personal Identifiable Information and Sensitive Information Stored on and Exchanged between Information Systems.” The project is expected to result in an ANSI-INCITS Technical Report. In the future, this document may be submitted as an input document to SC 27. The document will also take into account certain publications in the NIST SP 800 series and incorporate those aspects that apply to the scope of protection of personal identifiable information.

contents.html_ja: 国際的な取り組みに関しては、CS1 は、ISO/IEC JTC1 SC 27 のすべての国際セキュリティ標準プロジェクトに関する寄与の要請すべてに、一貫して、効率的に、適時に対応してきました。CS1 のメンバーによる寄与には、NIST の刊行物も含まれています。たとえば、FIPS 199 と 200 は、国際レベルで進行中の作業への寄与として引用されました。
contents.html: As regards international efforts, CS1 has consistently, efficiently, and in a timely manner responded to all calls for contributions on all international security standards projects in ISO/IEC JTC1 SC 27. Contributions from CS1 members have included NIST publications. For instance, FIPS 199 and 200 have been cited as contributions to ongoing work at the international level.

contents.html_ja: SP 800-114『User’s Guide to Securing External Devices for Telework and Remote Access』は、テレワーカーが、個人所有のデスクトップコンピュータやラップトップコンピュータ、民生用デバイス（たとえば、携帯電話、携帯情報端末［PDA］）など、テレワークに使用する外部デバイスを保護するのを支援することを目的としています。2007 年 6 月にパブリックコメント用に公開されたこの刊行物は、組織の非公開のコンピューティングリソースへのリモートアクセスを伴うテレワークのセキュリティに重点を置いています。テレワーク用コンピュータのオペレーティングシステムとアプリケーション、およびテレワーカーの自宅ネットワークを保護するための、実践的で現実に即した助言を提供し、民生用デバイスを保護するための基本的な推奨事項を示しています。また、この刊行物は、第三者が所有するデバイスをテレワークに使用すべきかどうかを決定する前に、そのセキュリティを評価するためのヒントも提供しています。
contents.html: SP 800-114, User’s Guide to Securing External Devices for Telework and Remote Access, is intended to help teleworkers secure the external devices they use for telework, such as personally owned desktop and laptop computers and consumer devices (e.g., cell phones, personal digital assistants [PDAs]). The publication, which was released for public comment in June 2007, focuses on security for telework involving remote access to an organization’s nonpublic computing resources. It provides practical, real-world advice on securing telework computers’ operating systems and applications and teleworkers’ home networks, and it gives basic recommendations for securing consumer devices. The publication also provides tips on assessing the security of a device owned by a third party before deciding whether it should be used for telework.

contents.html_ja: SP 800-113『Guide to SSL VPNs』は、2007 年 8 月にパブリックコメント用に公開されました。この文書は、組織が Secure Sockets Layer（SSL）仮想プライベートネットワーク（VPN）技術を理解するのを支援することを目指しています。この刊行物は、SSL VPN ソリューションの設計、実装、設定、保護、監視、保守についての推奨を示しています。SP 800-113 は、SSL VPN の展開を成功させるのに役立つ、SSL VPN の計画と実装への段階的アプローチを示しています。また、Internet Protocol Security（IPSec）VPN やその他の VPN ソリューションなど、他の類似技術との比較も含まれます。
contents.html: SP 800-113, Guide to SSL VPNs, was released for public comment in August 2007. It seeks to assist organizations in understanding Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) Virtual Private Network (VPN) technologies. The publication makes recommendations for designing, implementing, configuring, securing, monitoring, and maintaining SSL VPN solutions. SP 800-113 provides a phased approach to SSL VPN planning and implementation that can help in achieving successful SSL VPN deployments. It also includes a comparison with other similar technologies such as Internet Protocol Security (IPSec) VPNs and other VPN solutions.

contents.html_ja: SP 800-111『Guide to Storage Encryption Technologies for End User Devices』は、2007 年 8 月にパブリックコメント用に公開されました。この刊行物は、組織が、ラップトップ、PDA、スマートフォン、リムーバブルメディアなどのエンドユーザーデバイスのストレージ暗号化技術を理解し、ストレージ暗号化ソリューションを計画、実装、保守するのを支援することを目的としています。この刊行物は、ストレージ暗号化技法の 3 つの種類、すなわちフルディスク暗号化、ボリュームおよび仮想ディスクの暗号化、ファイル／フォルダーの暗号化について、実践的で現実に即した推奨事項を示しています。また、暗号鍵管理と認証を含む、ストレージ暗号化の展開の重要なセキュリティ要素についても論じています。
contents.html: SP 800-111, Guide to Storage Encryption Technologies for End User Devices, was released for public comment in August 2007. The publication is intended to assist organizations in understanding storage encryption technologies for end user devices, such as laptops, PDAs, smart phones, and removable media, and in planning, implementing, and maintaining storage encryption solutions. The publication provides practical, real-world recommendations for three classes of storage encryption techniques: full disk encryption, volume and virtual disk encryption, and file/folder encryption. It also discusses important security elements of a storage encryption deployment, including cryptographic key management and authentication.

contents.html: SP 800-101, Guidelines on Cell Phone Forensics, provides general principles and technical information to aid organizations in developing appropriate policies and procedures for preserving, acquiring, and examining digital evidence found on cell phones, and for reporting the results. Cell phones are an emerging but rapidly growing area of computer forensics. SP 800-101, which was published as final in June 2007, also explains the relationship between key aspects of cell phone technology and the operation and use of available forensic tools.

contents.html_ja: SP 900-98『Guidance for Securing Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) Systems』は、2007 年 4 月に最終版として公表されました。この刊行物は、組織が RFID 技術のリスクと、それらのリスクを低減するセキュリティ対策を理解するのを支援することを目指しています。セキュリティとプライバシーのリスクを低減する形で RFID ソリューションを開始、設計、実装、運用する方法について、実践的で現実に即したガイダンスを提供しています。また、RFID のセキュリティリスクと管理策の理解を助けるため、RFID のアプリケーション、標準、システム構成要素に関する背景情報も提供しています。この文書が示す情報は、特定のハードウェアプラットフォーム、オペレーティングシステム、アプリケーションには依存しません。産業界標準や国際標準に基づく RFID ソリューションに重点を置いていますが、現在の標準にはない関連するセキュリティ機能を提供する専有のアプローチが存在する場合は、その存在にも言及しています。
contents.html: SP 900-98, Guidance for Securing Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) Systems, was published as final in April 2007. This publication seeks to assist organizations in understanding the risks of RFID technology and security measures to mitigate those risks. It provides practical, real-world guidance on how to initiate, design, implement, and operate RFID solutions in a manner that mitigates security and privacy risks. The document also provides background information on RFID applications, standards, and system components to assist in the understanding of RFID security risks and controls. This document presents information that is independent of particular hardware platforms, operating systems, and applications. The emphasis is on RFID solutions that are based on industry and international standards, although the existence of proprietary approaches is noted when they offer relevant security features not found in current standards.

contents.html_ja: SP 800-97『Establishing Wireless Robust Security Networks: A Guide to IEEE 802.11i』は、2007 年 2 月に最終版として公表されました。この刊行物は、無線ローカルエリアネットワーク（WLAN）のセキュリティのための Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers（IEEE）802.11i 標準についての詳細な情報を提供しています。IEEE 802.11i は、これまでの 802.11 のセキュリティ方式である Wired Equivalent Privacy（WEP）に対するセキュリティの強化を提供します。WEP には、よく知られたセキュリティ上の欠陥がいくつもあります。IEEE 802.11i は、WEP の欠点を克服するように設計された、一連の新しいセキュリティ機能を導入しています。この文書は、これらのセキュリティ機能を説明し、WLAN 運用環境のセキュリティを確保するための具体的な推奨事項を示しています。WLAN 通信の機密性と完全性の保護、複数の方法を使ったユーザーとデバイスの認証、WLAN ライフサイクルの各フェーズへの WLAN セキュリティの考慮事項の組み込みについて、広範なガイダンスを提供しています。この文書は、次の文書に取って代わるものではなく、それらを補完するものです。NIST SP 800-48『Wireless Network Security: 802.11, Bluetooth and Handheld Devices』、および SP 800-48 改訂第 1 版『Wireless Network Security for IEEE 802.11a/b/g and Bluetooth』。
contents.html: SP 800-97, Establishing Wireless Robust Security Networks: A Guide to IEEE 802.11i, was published as final in February 2007. The publication provides detailed information on the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.11i standard for wireless local area network (WLAN) security. IEEE 802.11i provides security enhancements over the previous 802.11 security method, Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP), which has several well-documented security deficiencies. IEEE 802.11i introduces a range of new security features that are designed to overcome the shortcomings of WEP. This document explains these security features and provides specific recommendations to ensure the security of the WLAN operating environment. It gives extensive guidance on protecting the confidentiality and integrity of WLAN communications, authenticating users and devices using several methods, and incorporating WLAN security considerations into each phase of the WLAN life cycle. The document complements, and does not replace, NIST SP 800-48, Wireless Network Security: 802.11, Bluetooth and Handheld Devices, and SP 800-48 Revision 1, Wireless Network Security for IEEE 802.11a/b/g and Bluetooth.

contents.html_ja: SP 800-95『Guide to Secure Web Services』は、組織が、Web サービスに基づくサービス指向アーキテクチャ（SOA）の設計と開発に情報セキュリティのプラクティスを統合する際の課題を理解するのを支援することを目指しています。2007 年 8 月に最終版として公表された SP 800-95 は、Web サービスに適用される現在および新たな標準についての実践的で現実に即したガイダンスと、Web サービスに基づく SOA に対する最も一般的なセキュリティ上の脅威についての背景情報も提供しています。この文書が示す情報は、大部分が特定のハードウェアプラットフォーム、オペレーティングシステム、アプリケーションには依存しません。補助的なセキュリティデバイス（すなわち、境界セキュリティ機器）は、この刊行物の範囲外と見なされます。Web サービスの構成要素と補助的な管理策との間のインタフェースは、この文書全体を通じて、個別にその旨を記しています。
contents.html: SP 800-95, Guide to Secure Web Services, seeks to assist organizations in understanding the challenges in integrating information security practices into Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) design and development based on Web services. SP 800-95, which was published as final in August 2007, also provides practical, real-world guidance on current and emerging standards applicable to Web services, as well as background information on the most common security threats to SOAs based on Web services. This document presents information that is largely independent of particular hardware platforms, operating systems, and applications. Supplementary security devices (i.e., perimeter security appliances) are considered outside the scope of this publication. Interfaces between Web services components and supplementary controls are noted as such throughout this document on a case-by-case basis.

contents.html: SP 800-94, Guide to Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems (IDPS), was published as final in February 2007. It replaces SP 800-31, Intrusion Detection Systems. SP 800-94 provides guidelines for designing, implementing, configuring, securing, monitoring, and maintaining four classes of IDPS systems: network-based, wireless, network behavior analysis software, and host-based. It focuses on enterprise IDPS solutions, but most of the information in the publication is also applicable to standalone and small-scale IDPS deployments.

contents.html_ja: SP 800-61 改訂第 1 版『Computer Security Incident Handling Guide』は、2007 年 9 月にパブリックコメント用に公開されました。この文書は、インシデントに効果的かつ効率的に対応するための実践的なガイドラインを提供することにより、組織がコンピュータセキュリティインシデントによるリスクを低減するのを支援することを目指しています。この刊行物には、効果的なインシデント対応プログラムを確立するためのガイドラインが含まれていますが、この文書の主な重点は、インシデントの検知、分析、優先順位付け、対処です。SP 800-61 改訂第 1 版は、2004 年に公開された初版を更新するものです。
contents.html: SP 800-61 Revision 1, Computer Security Incident Handling Guide, was released for public comment in September 2007. It seeks to assist organizations in mitigating the risks from computer security incidents by providing practical guidelines on responding to incidents effectively and efficiently. The publication includes guidelines on establishing an effective incident response program, but the primary focus of the document is detecting, analyzing, prioritizing, and handling incidents. SP 800-61 Revision 1 updates the original publication, which was released in 2004.

SP 800-54 was published as final in July 2007.

contents.html: SP 800-48 Revision 1, Wireless Network Security for IEEE 802.11a/b/g and Bluetooth, was released for public comment in August 2007. The publication provides an overview of wireless networking technologies and gives detailed information on two standards commonly used in office environments and by mobile workforces: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.11a/b/g and IEEE 802.15.1, better known as Bluetooth. The publication seeks to assist organizations in reducing the risks associated with these forms of wireless networking. SP 800-48 Revision 1 updates the original version of SP 800-48, which was released in November 2002. SP 800-48 Revision 1 complements, and does not replace, SP 800-97, Establishing Wireless Robust Security Networks: A Guide to IEEE 802.11i. People seeking information on IEEE 802.11i should consult SP 800-97.

contents.html_ja: SP 800-45 バージョン 2『Guidelines on Electronic Mail Security』は、2007 年 2 月に最終版として公表されました。これは、2002 年に発行された元のガイドラインの更新であり、それに取って代わります。この刊行物は、組織が安全なメールサーバーとメールクライアントのインストール、設定、保守を行うのを支援することを目的としています。扱う話題には、電子メールの標準、電子メールの暗号化と署名、メールサーバーアプリケーションのセキュリティ、電子メールのコンテンツフィルタリングがあります。SP 800-45 バージョン 2 は、電子メールサーバーのオペレーティングシステム、アプリケーション、コンテンツ、およびそれを支えるネットワークインフラを保護するための推奨事項も示しています。
contents.html: SP 800-45 Version 2, Guidelines on Electronic Mail Security, was published as final in February 2007. It is an update to the original guideline issued in 2002, which it replaces. The publication is intended to aid organizations in the installation, configuration, and maintenance of secure mail servers and mail clients. Topics covered include e-mail standards, e-mail encryption and signing, mail server application security, and e-mail content filtering. SP 800-45, Version 2, also gives recommendations for securing the e-mail server operating systems, applications, and content as well as the supporting network infrastructure.

contents.html_ja: SP 800-44 バージョン 2『Guidelines on Securing Public Web Servers』は、2007 年 9 月に最終版として公表されました。SP 800-44 バージョン 2 は、組織が安全な公開 Web サーバーのインストール、設定、保守を行うのを支援することを目的としています。Web サーバーのオペレーティングシステム、アプリケーション、コンテンツの保護、支えとなるネットワークインフラを通じた Web サーバーの保護、Web サーバーの安全な管理についての推奨事項を示しています。SP 800-44 バージョン 2 は、Web サーバー上の情報を保護するために認証と暗号化の技術を使用することについてのガイドラインも示しています。この刊行物は、2002 年に公開された SP 800-44 の初版に取って代わるものです。
contents.html: SP 800-44, Version 2, Guidelines on Securing Public Web Servers, was published as final in September 2007. SP 800-44, Version 2 is intended to aid organizations in the installation, configuration, and maintenance of secure public Web servers. It presents recommendations for securing Web server operating systems, applications, and content; protecting Web servers through the supporting network infrastructure; and administering Web servers securely. SP 800-44, Version 2 also provides guidelines on using authentication and encryption technologies to protect information on Web servers. This publication replaces the original version of SP 800-44, which was released in 2002.

contents.html: SP 800-28, Version 2, Guidelines on Active Content and Mobile Code, was released for public comment in August 2007. This publication replaces the original version of SP 800-28, which was released in 2001.

contents.html_ja: NIST 省庁間報告書（NISTIR）7435『The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) and Its Applicability to Federal Agency Systems』は、2007 年 8 月に最終版として公表されました。CVSS は、IT の脆弱性の特性と影響を伝えるためのオープンな枠組みを提供します。この刊行物は、CVSS 標準を定義して説明し、スコアリングを行うための助言を提供し、特定の連邦機関の環境に合わせたスコアを生成するため、連邦機関が連邦情報処理標準（FIPS）199 の影響度の格付けを CVSS のスコアに取り込む方法を論じています。
contents.html: NIST Interagency Report (NISTIR) 7435, The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) and Its Applicability to Federal Agency Systems, was published as final in August 2007. CVSS provides an open framework for communicating the characteristics and impacts of IT vulnerabilities. This publication defines and describes the CVSS standard, provides advice on performing scoring, and discusses how federal agencies can incorporate Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) 199 impact ratings into their CVSS scores to generate scores that are specifically tailored to particular federal agency environments.

contents.html_ja: NISTIR 7387『Cell Phone Forensic Tools: An Overview and Analysis Update』は、携帯電話網対応の携帯端末に存在するデータの取得、調査、報告のために設計された現在のフォレンジックソフトウェアツールの概要を示しています。これは、この話題を最初に報告した NISTIR 7250 の後続の刊行物であり、いくつかの追加のツールを含んでいます。2007 年 6 月に最終版として公表された NISTIR 7387 は、シナリオベースの方法論を通じて、各ツールの能力と限界を詳しく検討しています。
contents.html: NISTIR 7387, Cell Phone Forensic Tools: An Overview and Analysis Update, provides an overview of current forensic software tools designed for the acquisition, examination, and reporting of data residing on cellular handheld devices. It is a follow-on publication to NISTIR 7250, which originally reported on the topic, and includes several additional tools. NISTIR 7387, which was published as final in June 2007, reviews the capabilities and limitations of each tool in detail through a scenario-based methodology.

contents.html_ja: NISTIR 7275 改訂第 2 版『Specification for the Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF) Version 1.1.3』は、2007 年 6 月に最終版として公表されました。この刊行物は、一連の対象システムに対するセキュリティ設定ルールの構造化された集合を保持するために使用できる、標準化された XML 形式である XCCDF を説明しています。XCCDF 仕様は、FISMA 準拠やその他の取り組みを支えられる、自動化された試験とスコアリングを提供するように設計されています。NISTIR 7275 は、XCCDF バージョン 1.1.3 のデータモデルと Extensible Markup Language（XML）表現を規定しています。NISTIR 7275 の前の改訂版は、XCCDF バージョン 1.1 を扱っていました。
contents.html: NISTIR 7275 Revision 2, Specification for the Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF) Version 1.1.3, was published as final in June 2007. The publication describes XCCDF, which is a standardized XML format that can be used to hold structured collections of security configuration rules for a set of target systems. The XCCDF specification is designed to provide automated testing and scoring that can support FISMA compliance and other efforts. NISTIR 7275 specifies the data model and Extensible Markup Language (XML) representation for version 1.1.3 of XCCDF; the previous revision of NISTIR 7275 addressed version 1.1 of XCCDF.

contents.html_ja: コンピュータセキュリティ部門の個人識別検証（PIV）チームは、国土安全保障に関する大統領令（HSPD）12 の実施に必要な標準、ガイドライン、試験プログラムを作成するリーダーシップにより、商務省の Gold Medal Award for Distinguished Service を受賞しました。この取り組みは、ばらばらの米国政府の要件をまとめ上げ、多様な技術上・政策上の関心を調整し、競合する技術を評価し、新しい相互運用性の方法を考案し、身元検証の改善された方法を開発することを必要としました。PIV チームの受賞者には、左から右に、William Polk、Donna Dodson、William Barker、Teresa Schwarzhoff、William MacGregor、Ramaswamy Chandramouli、James Dray、Hildegard Ferraiolo、そしてPatrick Grother がいます。写真に写っていないのは Timothy Grance です。
contents.html: The Computer Security Division’s Personal Identity Verification (PIV) Team was awarded the Department of Commerce Gold Medal Award for Distinguished Service for their leadership in producing the standards, guidelines, and test programs required to implement Homeland Security Presidential Directive (HSPD) 12. This effort required coalescing disparate United States Government requirements, reconciling diverse technical and policy interests, assessing competing technologies, inventing new methods of interoperability, and developing improved methods of identity verification. PIV team award recipients include, from left to right, William Polk, Donna Dodson, William Barker, Teresa Schwarzhoff, William MacGregor, Ramaswamy Chandramouli, James Dray, Hildegard Ferraiolo, and Patrick Grother. Not pictured is Timothy Grance.

contents.html_ja: William MacGregor は、上の写真で PIV チームの一員として写っており、Federal Computer Week により、2007 年の「Fed 100」賞の受賞者に選ばれました。この賞の審査員は、機関またはコミュニティ全体に顕著な違いをもたらした人物を探しています。MacGregor 氏は、国土安全保障大統領指令 12 に準拠するために連邦職員と請負業者が携帯しなければならない PIV カードについて、14 の標準とガイドラインを確立したチームを率いたことで表彰されました。彼のリーダーシップのもと、PIV チームは、カードのトポグラフィ、生体認証インタフェース、ミドルウェアと管理システムの標準と仕様を定める刊行物を作成しました。
contents.html: William MacGregor, pictured above as a member of the PIV team, was selected by Federal Computer Week to receive a 2007 “Fed 100” Award. The judges for these awards look for someone who has made a noticeable difference in an agency or in the community at large. Mr. MacGregor was recognized for leading the team that established 14 standards and guidelines for the PIV Card that federal employees and contractors are required to carry to comply with Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12. Under his leadership, the PIV team produced publications that defined the standards and specifications for the card topography, biometric interfaces, and middleware and management systems.

contents.html_ja: NIST は、さまざまな方法で産業界と学界の研究に資金を提供しています。Technology Innovation Program は、NIST の技術的専門領域における国家と社会の重要なニーズに対応する、潜在的に革新的な技術の研究について、産業界、大学、コンソーシアムに費用分担型の助成を提供します。Small Business Innovation Research Program は、中小企業からの研究開発の提案に資金を提供します。また、精密測定、火災研究、材料科学といった特定分野の取り組みを奨励するため、その他の助成金も提供しています。産業界、学界、その他の機関での研究を支援する助成金／賞は、NIST の複数の部署を通じて、競争的に利用できます。NIST の助成金プログラムの一般的な情報は、Ms. Melinda Chukran（(301) 975-5266、melinda.chukran@nist.gov）にお問い合わせください。
contents.html: NIST funds industrial and academic research in a variety of ways. Our Technology Innovation Program provides cost-shared awards to industry, universities, and consortia for research on potentially revolutionary technologies that address critical national and societal needs in NIST’s areas of technical competence. The Small Business Innovation Research Program funds R&D proposals from small businesses. We also offer other grants to encourage work in specific fields: precision measurement, fire research, and materials science. Grants/awards supporting research at industry, academia, and other institutions are available on a competitive basis through several different Institute offices. For general information on NIST grants programs, contact Ms. Melinda Chukran, (301) 975-5266, melinda.chukran@nist.gov.

As technology advances and requirements evolve, it is critical to evaluate existing standards, guidelines, and technologies to ensure that they adequately reflect the current state of the art. In FY 2007, CSD released the first public draft of Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 140-3 (Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules) to meet new and revised requirements for federal agency use of cryptographic systems, and to address technological and economic changes that have occurred since the issuance of FIPS 140-2 in 2001.

The primary goal of the Computer Security Division (CSD), a component of NIST’s Information Technology Laboratory (ITL), is to provide standards and technology that protects information systems against threats to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and services. During Fiscal Year 2007 (FY 2007), CSD successfully responded to numerous challenges and opportunities in fulfilling that mission. Through CSD’s diverse research agenda and engagement in many national priority initiatives, high-quality, cost-effective security mechanisms were developed and applied that improved information security across the federal government and the greater information security community.

original_blocks.html: In FY 2007, CSD continued to develop standards, metrics, tests, and validation programs to promote, measure, and validate security in systems and services. Recognizing the potential benefits of more automation in technical security operations, CSD established the Information Security Automation Program (ISAP), which is intended to formalize and advance efforts to enable the automation and standardization of technical security operations, including automated vulnerability management and policy compliance evaluations. The CSD also worked closely with federal agencies to improve their understanding of the Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) and supported a major intelligence community initiative to build a unified framework for information security across the federal government. This initiative is expected to result in greater standardization and more consistent and cost-effective security for all federal information systems.

original_blocks.html: The Information Security and Privacy Advisory Board (ISPAB) is a federal advisory committee that brings together senior professionals from industry, government, and academia to help advise the National Institute of Standards and Technology, the U.S. Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the Secretary of Commerce, and appropriate committees of the U.S. Congress about information security and privacy issues pertaining to unclassified federal government information systems.

original_blocks.html: The membership of the Board consists of 12 individuals and a Chairperson. The Director of NIST approves membership appointments and appoints the Chairperson. Each Board member serves for a four-year term. The Board’s membership draws from experience at all levels of information security and privacy work. The members’ careers cover government, industry, and academia. Members have worked in the Executive and Legislative branches of the federal government, civil service, senior executive service, the military, some of the largest corporations worldwide, small and medium-size businesses, and some of the top universities in the nation. The members’ experience, likewise, covers a broad spectrum of activities including many different engineering disciplines, computer programming, systems analysis, mathematics, management positions, information technology auditing, legal experience, an extensive history of professional publications, and professional journalism. Members have worked (and in many cases, continue to work in their full-time jobs) on the development and evolution of some of the most important pieces of information security and privacy legislation in the federal government, including the Privacy Act of 1974, the Computer Security Act of 1987, the E-Government Act (including FISMA), and numerous e-government services and initiatives.

NVLAP has received several applications for the accreditation of CMT Laboratories, which has resulted in the accreditation of one new U.S.-based CMT Laboratory in 2007 and one other laboratory in the accreditation process. This brings the current total number of accredited CMT Laboratories to 14, spanning locations in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Germany.

original_blocks.html: The CMVP and the CAVP are separate, collaborative programs based on a partnership between NIST’s Computer Security Division (CSD) and the Communication Security Establishment (CSE) of the Government of Canada. The programs provide federal agencies—in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom—with confidence that a validated cryptographic module meets a claimed level of security and that a validated cryptographic algorithm has been implemented correctly. The CMVP/CAVP validate modules and algorithms used in a wide variety of products including secure Internet browsers, secure radios, smart cards, space-based communications, munitions, security tokens, storage devices, and products supporting Public Key Infrastructure and electronic commerce. One module may be used in several products so that a small number of modules may account for hundreds of products. Likewise, the CAVP validates cryptographic algorithms that may be housed in one or more cryptographic modules.

The first draft of FIPS 140-3 underwent further development and research in FY 2006 as we reviewed the comments received and addressed the areas of the standard identified for improvement. Among the recommended changes were the stronger requirements on user authentication and data integrity verification, a new section focused on software modules, and the requirements to mitigate against noninvasive attacks that were not even feasible several years ago.

In July 2007, the first draft of the new FIPS 140-3 standard was released for public comment. This draft standard proposes increasing the number of security levels from four to five. Many other improvements have been introduced, reflecting the developing industry trends and our analysis of public’s comments. The comment period ended on October 11, 2007. This wasfollowedbyathoroughreviewandanalysisofallcomments. Depending on the nature of the received comments and suggestions, FIPS 140-3 may either be finalized or, more likely, a second draft of the standard will be developed. The second draft would then be made available to the public for comments, with the final version of the standard expected in early FY 2009.
The FIPS 140-3 standard will take effect six months after the final version is signed by the Secretary of Commerce.

original_blocks.html: Strategic goal 4
Devise advanced security methods, tools, and guidelines through conducting near-term
and midterm security research.
Overview

Our security research focus is to identify emerging technologies and conceive of new security solutions that will have a high impact on the critical information infrastructure. We perform research and development on behalf of government and industry from the earliest stages of technology development through proof-of-concept, reference and prototype implementations, and demonstrations. We work to transfer new technologies to industry, to produce new standards, and to develop tests, test methodologies, and assurance methods.

original_blocks.html: Our security research focus is to identify emerging technologies and conceive of new security solutions that will have a high impact on the critical information infrastructure. We perform research and development on behalf of government and industry from the earliest stages of technology development through proof-of-concept, reference and prototype implementations, and demonstrations. We work to transfer new technologies to industry, to produce new standards, and to develop tests, test methodologies, and assurance methods.

original_blocks.html: To keep pace with the rate of change in emerging technologies, we conduct a large amount of research in existing and emerging technology areas. Some of the many topics we research include smart card infrastructure and security, wireless and mobile device security, Voice over IP security issues, digital forensics tools and methods, access control and authorization management, Internet Protocol security, intrusion detection systems, quantum information system security and quantum cryptography, and vulnerability analysis. Our research helps to fulfill specific needs by the federal government that would not be easily or reliably filled otherwise.

original_blocks.html: Authentication of an individual’s identity is a fundamental component of physical and logical access control processes. When individuals attempt to access security-sensitive buildings, computer systems, or data, an access control decision must be made. An accurate determination of identity is an important step in making sound access control decisions. A wide range of mechanisms is employed to accurately determine identity; as a result, the strength of the authentication that is achieved varies, depending upon the type of credential, the process used to issue the credential, and the authentication mechanism used to validate the credential.

original_blocks.html: On August 27, 2004, the President signed Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12), entitled “Policy for a Common Identification Standard for Federal Employees and Contractors.” HSPD-12 requires the development and implementation of a governmentwide standard for secure and reliable forms of identification for federal employees and contractors. As required by HSPD-12, NIST issued FIPS 201, Personal Identity Verification (PIV) of Federal Employees and Contractors . Subsequently, NIST issued several Special Publications in support of FIPS 201.

The National Vulnerability Database (NVD) is the U.S. Government repository of standards-based vulnerability management data represented using the Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP). This data enables automation of vulnerability management, security measurement, and compliance checking. NVD includes databases of security checklists, security-related software flaws, misconfigurations, product dictionaries, and impact metrics. NVD is provided as a Web service that receives over 60 million hits per year, and its greatest use comes from computer security vendors downloading the NVD SCAP data and incorporating it into their products. NVD is sponsored by the Department of Homeland Security’s National Cyber Security Division.

original_blocks.html: Industrial control systems (ICSs) is a general term that encompasses several types of control systems, including supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems, distributed control systems (DCS), and other smaller control system configurations often found in the industrial control sectors. Our work focuses on SCADA systems and DCSs, which are used in the electric, water, oil and gas, chemical, transportation, pharmaceutical, pulp and paper, food and beverage, and discrete manufacturing (automotive, aerospace, and durable goods) industries.

original_blocks.html: SCADA systems are highly distributed systems used to control geographically dispersed assets, often scattered over thousands of square kilometers, where centralized data acquisition and control are critical to system operation. They are used in the distribution operations of water supply systems, oil and gas pipelines, electrical power grids, and railway transportation systems. A SCADA control center performs centralized monitoring and control for field sites over long-distance communications networks. This includes monitoring alarms and processing status data. Based on information received from remote stations, automated or operator-driven supervisory commands can be pushed to remote station control devices, which are often referred to as field devices. Field devices control local operations such as opening and closing valves and breakers, collecting data from sensor systems, and monitoring the local environment for alarm conditions.

original_blocks.html: DCSs are used to control industrial processes such as electric power generation, oil and gas refineries, wastewater treatment, and chemical, food, and automotive production. DCSs are integrated as a control architecture containing a supervisory level of control overseeing multiple, integrated subsystems that are responsible for controlling the details of a localized process. DCSs are used extensively in process-based industries.

original_blocks.html: Most ICSs in use today were developed years ago, long before public and private networks, desktop computing, or the Internet were a common part of business operations. These systems were designed to meet performance, reliability, safety, and flexibility requirements and were typically physically isolated and based on proprietary hardware, software, and communication protocols. These proprietary communication protocols included basic error detection and correction capabilities, but nothing that guaranteed secure communications. The need for cyber security measures within these systems was not anticipated, and at the time, security for ICSs meant physically securing access to the network and the consoles that controlled the systems.

original_blocks.html: As microprocessor, personal computer, and networking technology evolved during the 1980s and 1990s, the design of ICSs changed to incorporate the latest technologies. Internet-based technologies started making their way into ICS designs in the late 1990s. These changes to ICSs exposed them to new types of threats and significantly increased the likelihood that they would be attacked. While security solutions have been designed to deal with these security issues in typical IT systems, special precautions must be taken when introducing these same solutions to ICS environments. In some cases, new IT security solutions are needed.

original_blocks.html: In the past year, we have collaborated with the NIST Manufacturing Engineering Laboratory (MEL) in developing a guide to ICS security, draft NIST SP 800-82, Guide to Industrial Control Systems (ICS) Security: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Systems, Distributed Control Systems (DCS), and Other Control System Configurations Such as Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC). The purpose of this document is to provide guidance for establishing secure SCADA systems and other ICSs. The document provides an overview of ICSs and typical system topologies, identifies typical vulnerabilities and threats to these systems, and provides recommended security countermeasures to mitigate the associated risks. The second public draft of SP 800-82 was released in September 2007, and the final document is expected to be completed in early 2008. This guideline is being prepared for use by federal agencies, but it may be used by nongovernmental organizations on a voluntary basis.

Securing the Domain Name System (DNS)

The Domain Name System (DNS) is the method by which Internet addresses in mnemonic form such as http://csrc.nist.gov are converted into the equivalent numeric Internet Protocol (IP) addresses such as 129.6.13.39. Certain servers throughout the world maintain the databases needed, as well as perform the translations. A DNS server trying to perform a translation may communicate with other Internet DNS servers if it does not have the data needed to translate the address itself.

Like any other Internet-based system, DNS is subject to several threats. To counter these threats, the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF)—an international standards body—came up with a set of specifications for securing DNS called DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC). In partnership with the Department of Homeland Security, we have been actively involved in promoting the deployment of DNSSEC since 2004.
